title: wowtomate consumes ui_base instead of its own copies
acceptance_criteria: wowtomate/tools/review_ui no longer contains menu.js, shell.js, align.js or app.css; its server serves those from ui_base.read_asset; the review tool looks and behaves identically, and tests/test_review_server.py still passes every route, id and script check
notes: THIS IS WHAT PROVES THE SEAM IS REAL rather than assumed. Deliberately not done on extraction day: wowtomate had just been heavily refactored and was in daily use. TWO THINGS TO HANDLE. (1) token renames - ui_base calls them --accent-on/--muted-on where wowtomate's app.css said --keep-on/--discard-on, so tabs.css and app.js references move with it. (2) the dependency direction: wowtomate would gain a local path dependency on ui_base, so it can no longer be cloned standalone. That is an architectural call for Fabian, not something to assume. DONE 2026-09-02. wowtomate takes ui-base as an editable path dependency ([tool.uv.sources]) and its review server serves /ui/ local-first: review_ui/ wins, ui_base fills in. menu.js, shell.js and align.js deleted from wowtomate. THE EXTRACTION HELD: the three copies differed ONLY in comments (wowtomate's named kernels and nameplates, ui_base's are generalised) - every line of code was identical, so nothing had to be reconciled. ui_base's requires-python went 3.12 -> 3.11 to match wowtomate, which was the only real friction. CSS deliberately NOT merged: wowtomate has app.css + tabs.css where ui_base has base.css, and unifying them is a visual change nobody asked for - that is task 2's territory.

title: a second consumer, to find what is still wowtomate-shaped
acceptance_criteria: a project that is not wowtomate builds a working two-tab page on ui_base without editing any file under ui_base/assets
notes: one consumer cannot tell you what is general. The demo is a weak second consumer - it was written by the same hand, on the same day, against the same assumptions. The fish gate project (see ~/Documents/dev/ai_lab/fish-gate-cnn-guide.md) is the real candidate.

title: no test suite yet
acceptance_criteria: read_asset's traversal refusal is pinned by a test, and a headless check asserts the demo page's scripts parse and every API it calls exists
notes: checked BY HAND on extraction day and both passed: ../pyproject.toml and a url-encoded traversal both 404, and every function and section kind the demo uses exists with matching option names. Hand-checked is not pinned - the demo drifting from the assets is the failure that would make the README quietly wrong. DONE 2026-09-02. tests/test_assets.py, 16 tests. Three groups, one per failure this package can actually have: serving what it should not (traversal, symlink escape, all parametrised), failing to serve what a consumer links (EXPECTED named explicitly, never globbed - a test that reads the directory it checks passes on an empty directory), and shipping broken assets (node --check on every script; every var() resolves to a token the file defines; every token exists on bare :root, since the default 'system' theme stamps no attribute and a token defined only under a media query is undefined for most viewers).
